moments.frontstage: Business online banking marketing only: 'Access ACH payments for free and send wires. Pay your business bills and invoices, all in one place.' The only published SMB vendor-payment step sequence is Accounts Payable with Capital One: 'Manage Accounts Payable' tab above transaction history > 'Add Business Bill' > pay 'with your Capital One Business card or an ACH bank transfer' > vendor receives 'a paper check or a bank transfer' > deduction date + delivery speed > 'Confirm'; tracks 'scheduled, upcoming and past payments'. Whether standard business-checking ACH uses this flow is not stated.

moments.title: Single-user authorization: standard Capital One Business online banking…
moments.customer_action: Single-user authorization: standard Capital One Business online banking offers user delegation ('Manage Account Users') and alerts but no maker/checker; 'Dual Control Authorization' (one user creates, another approves before transmission) exists only for payments made via Intellix, i.e., by adopting treasury management (included with Premier Checking)

moments.title: Returns / unauthorized ACH
moments.frontstage: Small-business deposit rules: 'Errors involving ACH entries must be reported to Bank immediately' so Bank can act within 'the time frame for return requests under the Nacha Rules' — late requests may not be accepted and 'Customer could incur Losses' (§6.7); other errors must be reported in writing within 30 days of the statement (§4.1). For outgoing payments that are returned, 'Bank has no obligation to separately notify Customer' and 'it will be Customer's responsibility to resubmit the Payment Order' (§6.4). Treasury clients can add ACH Debit Protection (TM schedule).

exceptions.trigger: Unauthorized or erroneous ACH entry on business account
exceptions.bank_handling: Rules §6.7: Bank acts within Nacha return time frames; late requests may not be honored; §4.1 written notice within 30 days for other errors
exceptions.resolution: Return if timely; otherwise customer bears losses

assessment: Capability exists but SMB payment journeys are the least documented area on capitalone.com.

terms.fees: ACH free on named accounts; others may incur fees
